doc.name: A — small appliance catalogue, archive shelving, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: espresso machine portafilter
Category: small appliance
Shot programme: archive shelving
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You run the tabletop stage for a premium small appliance product shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the floating levitation in an archive shelving treatment.

SUBJECT. A espresso machine portafilter. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Product suspended mid-air with no visible support and a soft drop shadow beneath. Shoot on a 50mm normal at f/8, framing for deep negative space above the subject with a low horizon.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a ring light on axis for flat, modern, shadowless coverage. Stage the product on or against cracked dry clay, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a clean high-key grade with the whites pushed to the edge of clipping. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Your entire reply is the prompt itself: one dense paragraph, no title, no quotation marks, no trailing notes.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
